notes.title: 약속
notes.text: 약속 means both "promise" and "plans to meet": 약속 있어요 = "I have plans." Kids seal promises by hooking pinkies and pressing thumbs together — a "stamp."

notes.title: Weather on TV
notes.text: Korean news uses formal endings: 맑겠습니다 ("it will be clear"), 비가 오겠습니다 ("it will rain"). In conversation you'd say 맑을 거예요 and 비가 올 거예요.

notes.title: 첫눈
notes.text: The first snow of the year (첫눈) is romantic in Korea: friends and couples promise to meet when it falls, and it's a classic K-drama moment. Keep an eye out for it in this story…

notes.title: Seeing Korea
notes.text: Busan (부산) is Korea's second city, famous for beaches and seafood. Jeju Island (제주도) is a volcanic island and honeymoon spot. Gyeongju (경주) was the capital of the Silla kingdom for nearly a thousand years.

Let's go to Jeju together next year!

talk.cue: Say good, let's go next year.
b: to be good, to be nice

notes.title: Arriving in Korea
notes.text: Most international flights land at Incheon Airport (인천공항), about an hour from central Seoul by the airport railroad (공항철도).
